Subject: Purchasing via AWS/Azure/GCP marketplaces — next steps

Hi Marissa,

We're evaluating Redwood for a cross-product pilot and our procurement team prefers purchasing through a cloud marketplace (AWS or Azure preferred). Can you confirm: 1) whether Redwood supports marketplace invoicing (AWS Marketplace or Azure Marketplace purchase flow) with consolidated billing and an upper-tier seller listing; 2) if PO-based procurement is supported through those marketplaces or if we need a direct PO to Redwood; and 3) any lead time or paperwork required (seller agreement, tax forms, POC setup) for a Q1 contract start.

If it helps, procurement attached the PO template they typically use. Looking to close procurement path decision this week.

Thanks,

Hi Emily — thanks for the note and the PO template. Short answers up front: we support purchases via AWS Marketplace (including SaaS contracts and private offers) and Azure Marketplace in many cases; GCP marketplace is possible but more involved. PO-based procurement can be done either via the marketplace private offer flow (customer issues PO to AWS/Azure which channels payment to us) or directly to Redwood (we accept POs and invoice). There are tradeoffs for each approach around payment timing and invoice visibility.

I'll loop in our Sales Ops and Legal to confirm specific docs and lead times. Connor — can you confirm whether the BrightApps template works for a marketplace private offer or whether Legal will need an amended version? Grace — please check typical lead time for AWS private offer activation.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Team — forwarding BrightApps' questions. Proposed plan:
1) Confirm legal accepts BrightApps_PO_Template.pdf or provide small redlines (usually payment remittance, indemnity language, termination notice).
2) If BrightApps wants marketplace private offer (preferred), we open a private offer request via AWS Marketplace (we need account seller ID and expected SKUs/pricing). AWS private offers typically take 5-7 business days for processing once submitted; Azure is similar.
3) For net-30 terms via marketplace, we typically provide private offers with invoicing through our finance partner (we have marketplace private offer templates that preserve net-30; marketplace fees are visible as a separate line in some invoices).
4) Compliance: BrightApps asking for SOC 2 Type II, AMS listing evidence — Monica, can you prepare a redacted SOC 2 PDF and the seller verification checklist?

Grace — can you confirm average SLA for AWS private offer activation and whether we can preserve BrightApps' PO number on the invoice?

Connor
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

Connor / team — details below based on recent marketplace activations:
- AWS private offer turnaround: 3-8 business days (depends on accounting verification). We can usually expedite to 2-3 days if legal and price are finalized and AWS has the seller registration in good standing.
- Marketplace fees: AWS fees (seller fees) are charged on top of the gross sale in their reporting, but for private offers we can set pricing so BrightApps sees a single line item equal to the final customer price; marketplace fees show in settlement statements, not on the customer-facing invoice unless explicitly itemized. Finance can preserve the customer PO number on the AWS invoice/meta fields — we just need the PO up front.
- Required docs: redacted SOC 2, W9/Q10 tax docs, Redwood Marketplace Seller Agreement (attached).

Monica — please attach redacted SOC2 and the Seller Agreement for Marissa to send to BrightApps.

Grace
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Hi Emily — thanks for the clarifying questions. Below is a concise marketplace procurement path and what we need from BrightApps to move forward: 

1) Preferred path: AWS Marketplace private offer (keeps procurement within AWS with consolidated billing).
   - What we need from you: completed PO (use your template), desired term (12 months), contact for signing, and the BrightApps legal entity tax info.
   - Timeline: once we have signed pricing and the PO, AWS activation typically 3–7 business days.

2) Alternate path: Direct PO to Redwood (we invoice BrightApps directly).
   - What we need: PO + W9 + signature on Redwood Marketplace Seller Agreement (attached). Invoicing net-30 possible.

3) Marketplace fees & pricing: We'll set the private offer so the final customer price matches the PO line-item. AWS settlement will show marketplace fees but these do not change the amount you pay. If you require explicit marketplace fee line items, note that in the PO.

4) Compliance: attached redacted SOC 2 Type II and our seller agreement.

Next steps: Emily — if you confirm AWS private offer, reply with the PO and the entity name for the seller verification. We'll generate a private offer and send a DocuSign for signature if any contract redlines are needed. I've attached: AWS_Procurement_Checklist.pdf, Redwood_Marketplace_Seller_Agreement.pdf, BrightApps_PO_Template.pdf.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that's easier to close the path this week.

Best,
